body.statement: Uniformly over \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{global,reg}}\), if the unique prefix \(k_n^{\star}\) satisfies \(\min_{l\ne k_n^{\star}}\{\mathfrak r_{n,l}-\mathfrak r_{n,k_n^{\star}}\}\ge\varepsilon\), then \(\mathbb P_n(\widehat k_n=k_n^{\star})\to1\) and the bounded-Lipschitz distance between the law of \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{n,\widehat k_n}-\tau_n-b_{n,k_n^{\star}})\) and \(N(0,\Gamma_n(k_n^{\star},k_n^{\star}))\) tends to zero. This is Yang, Li, Wu, and Yang's fixed positive unscaled-MSE regime as a consequence of the generated-prefix joint expansion.
body.justification: The fixed-gap reduction verifies that the boundary theory nests the familiar oracle regime rather than replacing it with an unrelated asymptotic experiment.
body.gap: Yang, Li, Wu, and Yang state the oracle selection conclusion under fixed separation; the additional content is its derivation as the diverging-gap face of the joint generated-prefix law.
body.consumer: Practitioners can recover ordinary single-prefix inference when the empirical selector is genuinely stable.
